newsitem.title: USA: Oil-Dri sees benefits of new products.
newsitem.headline: Oil-Dri sees benefits of new products.

text.p: Oil-Dri Corp of America said on Friday it benefited in the first quarter from outlays last year in its consumer business and product introductions.

"The benefits of last year's investment in our consumer business and the new products launch were evident in the quarter," said Richard Jaffee, chairman and chief executive officer, in a statement. "Specialty product sales were strong and industrial and environmental profitability was up."

The company, which makes and sells absorbent products for consumer, industrial, environmental, agricultural and fluid purification markets, reported first-quarter net earnings per share of $0.29 versus $0.21 in the year-earlier period.

He said marketing and advertising investment in 1995 for Cat's Pride cat litter was "paying off" in higher sales and profits despite a drop of about $2.0 million in first-quarter sales to Sam's Club. The chain chose to offer Cat's Pride Premium and a private-label brand that Oil-Dri does not make.
"We are particularly gratified to see the growth in the consumer products division in light of the decreased revenues with this account," he added.
He said the company saw a "strong" agricultural season and "continued contributions" from fluid purification and industrial/environmental units.
